questions.stem: Why do hormones only affect specific target cells?

options.text: Because hormones can only travel to certain parts of the body
Because only target cells have the specific receptors that match the hormone
Because the blood only flows to target organs
Because other cells destroy the hormone before it can act

questions.explanation: Hormones travel throughout the body in the blood, but they only affect target cells that have specific receptors complementary to the hormone's shape, similar to a lock and key mechanism.
